title: Finite-free lisse sheaves are site-perfect, flat and constructible
statement: Fix l, E, n and A as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], a scheme S and a sheaf L of A-modules on S_et that is etale locally isomorphic to a constant sheaf A^t (t≥0 depending on the member of the covering) [def-sf-finite-free-hom-evaluation-coordinates]. Then the degree-zero complex L[0] in the unbounded derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] is site-perfect [def-sf-etale-site-perfect-complex], has Tor amplitude in [0,0] [def-kun-tor-amplitude], and is bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

source.place: Paragraphs 2–3, lisse degree-zero specialization of the site-perfect stratum argument

proof.text: On each member of the covering the restriction of L[0] is isomorphic to the single complex of the constant sheaf A^t, a bounded complex whose terms are retracts of finite free constant sheaves; this is the site-perfectness witness of [def-sf-etale-site-perfect-complex].

source.place: Paragraphs 2–3, lisse degree-zero specialization of the site-perfect stratum argument

proof.text: Every geometric point lifts to a member of the covering; there the stalk of L is A^t, which is flat. Hence L is flat, and a flat sheaf placed in degree zero has Tor amplitude [0,0] [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

source.place: Paragraphs 2–3, lisse degree-zero specialization of the site-perfect stratum argument

proof.text: L is locally constant with finite stalks, hence constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]; a single constructible sheaf is bounded constructible.

source.place: Paragraphs 2–3, lisse degree-zero specialization of the site-perfect stratum argument
